added.title: Summer 2027 Internship Program:  Machine Learning Engineering - Brooklyn, NY
added.description:
Our Gridtern Program provides currently enrolled college students with the opportunity to gain practical experience in the energy industry.

This posting represents a specific internship opportunity supporting the Machine Learning Engineering team in Brooklyn, NY.

What You’ll Do

Our Machine Learning Engineering team is responsible for building and maintaining National Grid's AI Platform. This team helps to develop various data pipelines that power machine learning solutions, help bring data science models into production, supports cloud infrastructure in Azure, and builds the tools and platforms used by data scientists and engineers across the organization.

As a Gridtern, you will work alongside Machine Learning Engineers and Data Scientists to help build and maintain National Grid's AI Platform. You will contribute to machine learning projects, develop tools that support the Data Science team, collaborate on data pipelines that power data-driven solutions, and assist with deploying machine learning models into production environments. Additionally, you will also gain hands-on experience with technologies such as Python, SQL, Azure, GitHub, Docker, Kubernetes, and Airflow while developing technical skills, learning software engineering best practices, and contributing to projects that deliver real business impact.

You will be based in Brooklyn, NY and must reside within a commutable distance to the designated work location during this period.

What You'll Need to Apply

Availability to start on the program start date, Monday, May 24, 2027, and work full-time (40 hours a week) for the duration of the summer
Must be registered as a full-time student and continue your education full-time through the Fall 2027 semester
Pursuing an Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Machine Learning Engineering, Information Systems, Mathematics, or a related field
Have accumulated 18 or more credits and be at least 18 years of age
Possess work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States (including CPT & OPT)
Valid US Driver’s license with a safe driving history that complies with National Grid’s Safe Driver policy.

What You’ll Get in Return

Gain hands-on experience applying your academic knowledge to meaningful work
Explore career opportunities and build your understanding of the energy industry
Connect with professionals across National Grid and expand your network
Receive personalized feedback, coaching, and mentorship throughout your internship
Develop the confidence, skills, and experience needed to launch your career
An hourly wage based on your major, degree type, and class year

About The Intern Program

Your summer will begin on Monday, May 24, 2027
. Our Gridtern Program offers you the chance to expand your skills and broaden your mind, while exploring the best of what our industry has to offer.

You’ll work full time with a specific team for the duration of your internship, taking part in training and development activities to kickstart your career.

About National Grid

National Grid is the critical energy infrastructure company, operating the electricity and gas networks and infrastructures that connects millions of people to the energy they use every day, supporting homes, businesses and communities across Massachusetts and New York.

We know the future of energy won't be shaped by what we know today. It will be shaped by what's possible tomorrow. That's why we're investing in the next generation of talent, giving undergraduates and graduates the opportunity to learn from experts, gain hands-on experience and contribute to work that matters from day one.

Are you ready to unlock the power of the possible?

More Information

Salary Range

$22.00 -$28.00 an hour

National Grid will not be providing visa sponsorship for this position now or in the future. You must have the ability to work without a need for current or future visa sponsorship.

Candidates will be assessed and provided offers based on major, degree type, and class year. Our Gridtern Program does not offer relocation, housing assistance, or public transportation reimbursement for Gridterns; however, we can provide a list of resources to utilize in making your arrangements.

Please note that as a Gridtern, you must reside within our existing footprint, which includes Massachusetts, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Maine, Rhode Island, and Vermont. added.title: Graduate Development Program, Associate Engineer, Software Engineering
added.description:
About The Position

Are you ready to build software that helps support National Grid’s Gas business? As an Associate Software Engineer, you’ll join the team responsible for the development and support of the software that enables gas operations. The tools you help maintain are used by field technicians to find work locations, access job details, complete work safely, and close out work orders. In other words, your work helps support the systems that allow trucks to get into the field and teams to maintain critical gas infrastructure.

You’ll work alongside experienced engineers, architects, product teams, and business stakeholders to deliver feature enhancements, fix bugs, test changes, and improve the reliability of our software. This is a great opportunity to build your software engineering skills while gaining experience with SaaS platforms, modern web development, and real-world business applications.

What You'll Do

Develop, test, maintain, and enhance application features using modern programming languages and frameworks including React, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
Apply object-oriented programming (OOP) principles such as encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.
Develop reusable, maintainable, and well-structured software components.
Work with REST APIs and integrate front-end applications with backend services.
Write unit tests and participate in code reviews.
Debug application issues and assist with root-cause analysis.
Use Git and established source control and CI/CD practices.
Participate in Agile development activities, including sprint planning, refinement, and retrospectives.
Collaborate with senior engineers and architects to understand technical designs and development standards.
Create and maintain appropriate technical documentation.

What You'll Need to Apply

Bachelor or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field from an accredited institution
Graduated between May 2026 and June 2027
Ability to begin the National Grid Graduate Program on June 7, 2027, or July 12, 2027
Work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States (such as sponsorship for an H-1B, TN, O, L, STEM OPT, or other employment-based work authorization)
Foundational knowledge of object-oriented programming and software design principles.
Programming experience with at least one object-oriented language, such as Java, Apex, or Python.
Experience or coursework developing user interfaces with React or a similar modern JavaScript framework.
Working knowledge of JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
A basic understanding of REST APIs, JSON, and client-server application architecture.
Familiarity with Git or another source control platform.
An understanding of the software development lifecycle and Agile development practices.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.

It would be awesome if you had

Exposure to SaaS platforms, including Salesforce or similar tools.
Familiarity with automated testing frameworks.
Exposure to CI/CD tools such as GitHub Actions or similar platforms.
A basic understanding of cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure or AWS.
Experience with SQL, relational databases, or NoSQL databases.

What You’ll Get in Return

Structured development opportunities, mentorship, and ongoing feedback to accelerate your career growth
Exposure to leaders, cross-functional teams, and diverse areas of the business
Opportunities to build your professional network and develop lasting industry connections
Meaningful work and real-world experience that provide a strong foundation for a long-term career at National Grid
Competitive salary ranging from $73,000 to $102,000, plus a comprehensive benefits package
Financial support for your future through up to $6,000 in student loan repayment assistance and tuition reimbursement benefits of up to $8,000 annually for undergraduate studies and $10,000 annually for graduate studies
The ability to build technical skills through hands-on development, training, and mentoring.
The opportunity to contribute to the systems that help field technicians locate work, complete assignments, and maintain critical gas infrastructure.

About The Graduate Development Program

National Grid’s Graduate Development Program (GDP) is a year-long development program for recent college graduates who aspire to take on future leadership roles in a dynamic, ever-changing industry. Graduates will shape the future of National Grid. Bringing fresh thinking, new perspectives, and exploring with energy, we’ll give you real responsibility and an opportunity to move with purpose from day one – putting the power to supercharge your career in your hands.

Graduates start their careers at National Grid with an in-depth 3-week in-person Orientation which gives you exposure to all parts of the company, allows you to network with your Graduate cohort, GDP alumni, and senior leaders, and provides you with the opportunity to travel throughout our service territory in the northeast US. Following Orientation, you’ll begin working in the full-time position outlined below and take part in robust in-person and virtual development activities throughout the year. This includes monthly development sessions, active mentorship, and an intensive and immersive “Hackathon Project” where you “hack” a real-world National Grid problem.

GDP Information Technology & Digital Rotations

In Technology & Innovation, we’re working at the heart of change and harnessing the power of technology to build a cleaner, fairer, and more affordable future for all. Innovation is providing our edge in finding a better way for everyone. In fact, we like to think of ourselves as a band of unsung heroes. Our IT Graduate Development Rotational Program will provide you with the opportunity to be at the heart of this transformation. The program consists of an 18-month exploration consisting of three 6-month rotations in varying IT & Digital departments. Your ﬁrst rotation will be in the role outlined below and you will return to this role following two broadening 6-month rotations where you will solve complex problems and focus on growth that will transform the energy sector as we know it.

We know the future of energy won't be shaped by what we know today. It will be shaped by what's possible tomorrow. That's why we're investing in the next generation of talent, giving undergraduates and graduates the opportunity to learn from experts, gain hands-on experience and contribute to work that matters from day one.

added.title: Software Engineer (Scientific Computing)
added.description:
At Areté, we are on the forefront of developing innovative solutions, with great minds from all backgrounds, to help solve the nation’s most complex security challenges. We strive for an inclusive, collaborative team environment that approaches differences as opportunities for innovation and excellence. As an employee-owned company, we foster an atmosphere that propels diverse career opportunities and professional growth.

Discover your future with us.

We are seeking a junior to mid-level applicant with a background in Scientific Computing. The ideal person would have a degree in Physics, Math, or Engineering coupled with a strong software development skillset. added.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About Our Science Teams

We are looking for an ML Software Engineer to join the Multi-Embodiment Generalist Agent (MEGA) team within Wayve Science as a founding member. MEGA is building foundation models for general-purpose robots: models that learn from large-scale video, language, and robot-interaction data, then generalize across tasks and embodiments, including mobile manipulators, dual-arm platforms, and humanoids. Our aim is to build agents that can perceive, reason about, and act reliably in the physical world. You will design and build the software systems that enable MEGA’s machine learning research. This includes scalable ML pipelines, data and training infrastructure, and the shared tools and abstractions that allow researchers to move quickly from an idea to a reliable experiment. The role sits close to the models and data. You will work with large-scale video and robotics datasets, modern ML frameworks, and increasingly large models, building systems that remain reliable and maintainable as the research program grows. You will be a core member of the MEGA team, owning key parts of the software and ML infrastructure that underpin the research program, and will help shape how the team develops and operates its ML stack as the program grows.

🧠 Your day-to-day

Design and maintain scalable pipelines for data ingestion, model training, evaluation, and experimentation.
Build reusable interfaces and shared tooling across data, models, training, evaluation, and downstream robotics workflows.
Partner with researchers to translate evolving model and experiment needs into practical software systems.
Diagnose and resolve performance, reliability, and usability bottlenecks across large-scale ML workloads.
Raise the quality of the shared codebase through strong architecture, testing, documentation, and engineering standards.
Support distributed training and data processing across large video, language, and robot-interaction datasets.

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Design, build, and maintain scalable ML pipelines for data ingestion, model training, evaluation, and related research workflows.
Build software systems that allow ML workloads to scale to larger datasets, larger models, and more experiments.
Develop clean and reusable interfaces between data, models, training, evaluation, and downstream robotics workflows.
Own and improve the health of the MEGA codebase, including software architecture, testing, reliability, maintainability, and engineering standards.
Identify and resolve performance, reliability, and usability bottlenecks across ML workflows.
Build and maintain infrastructure that supports multiple researchers and ML projects without unnecessarily slowing down iteration.
Work closely with researchers to understand the requirements of new models and experiments, and translate those requirements into practical software solutions.
Build and use distributed training and data-processing pipelines for large models and large multimodal datasets.

🙌 You should apply if

Strong software engineering skills and experience building high-quality, maintainable software.
Experience building and maintaining machine learning pipelines or infrastructure, such as data ingestion, training, evaluation, or experiment workflows.
Experience designing software systems and abstractions that are reliable, reusable, and able to evolve as requirements change.
Hands-on experience with modern machine learning frameworks and a good understanding of how ML training and experimentation workflows operate.
Strong debugging skills and the ability to investigate problems across complex ML systems.
Experience with software testing, code quality, and engineering practices for maintaining a healthy shared codebase.
Experience working with large datasets, large models, or other computationally demanding ML workloads.
Ability to collaborate closely with researchers and engineers and translate research requirements into practical software systems.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)
Competency Interviews (Programming and hiring manager interview; 1.5 hours total)
Deep-dive technical interviews (Systems & domain-specific interviews; 3 hours total)

added.title: Software Engineer, Fleet Management
added.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About Our Engineering Teams

Our Fleet Management team builds the platform that connects Wayve’s engineers and operators with a global fleet of autonomous vehicles and data-collection devices. From software deployment and vehicle health to robotaxi operations, our services give teams the visibility and control they need to operate confidently as the fleet grows.

You’ll join an early-stage team working across web applications, backend services, embedded APIs and cloud infrastructure. With multiple OEM integrations and vehicle configurations to support, you’ll help shape both the systems we build and the engineering practices behind them.

🧠 Your day-to-day

Own full-stack features, working with senior engineers, Product Managers and Designers to turn agreed designs into production-quality software.
Contribute to technical discussions and break work into practical implementation steps.
Follow your work through testing, deployment and maintenance.
Write clean, performant code, debug issues and review peers’ changes.
Share what you learn and take on more complex problems as your experience grows.
Keep usability and reliability central to the tools you build for real vehicle operations.

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Frontend and backend features that help teams understand fleet health, configuration, software status and location.
APIs, databases and cloud services behind Fleet Management workflows.
Tools that support engineers and operators across different OEMs and vehicle configurations.
Scalable, maintainable services developed in partnership with senior engineers.
Automated tests, debugging and code reviews that improve the quality and consistency of the platform.

🙌 You should apply if

You have professional experience building full-stack web applications or services, with genuine hands-on exposure to both frontend and backend development.
You have worked with APIs, schemas, databases and backend services.
You can deliver clean, tested and maintainable code, and contribute thoughtfully to technical design discussions.
You are familiar with cloud services, distributed systems or microservice architectures.
You take ownership of assigned work, communicate proactively and enjoy learning from experienced teammates.
Experience with React, TypeScript, MUI, Rust, Go, Node.js, Kubernetes, Bazel or Azure would be useful, but not required.
Bonus if you have experience with fleet management, robotics, autonomy, operational tooling, monitoring or high-volume data workflows.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins).
Competency Interviews: Programing and Domain Knowledge (3 hours ).
Deep-dive technical interviews: System Design and Hiring Manager Interview (1,5 hour in total).
Final interview: Mission & Values alignment (30 mins).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve

✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

added.title: Site Reliability Engineer, Vehicle Software
added.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About Our Vehicle Software Engineering Teams

Our Vehicle Software Engineering team builds and operates the software that keeps Wayve’s autonomous vehicles running safely in the real world. Within it, the Tools & Infrastructure team owns the reliability stack for vehicle software: observability, incident management, operator tooling, and the automation that lets engineering and operations detect and resolve issues faster. As Wayve scales its autonomous vehicle programs with OEM partners this team is defining what SRE looks like for vehicle-centric systems from the ground up.

🧠 Your day-to-day

Building and improving tooling, automation, observability, and incident-management processes for vehicle software reliability
Partnering closely with field engineers, software teams, and operations to diagnose reliability issues and improve system performance
Owning hands-on debugging across Linux, low-level systems, logs, metrics, traces, and vehicle and production data
Developing reliability improvements that reduce manual intervention and make issue detection, triage, and recovery faster
Supporting vehicle-centric operations, including safety-operator tools and the reliability needs of our customer and partner programmes

🧩 What You’ll Be Working On

Reliability for real-world autonomous vehicle operations, not just traditional cloud or platform SRE
Vehicle safety, operator tooling, observability, and incident management that have a direct impact on production reliability
Close collaboration with software engineering, operations, and field teams to improve how issues are detected, triaged, and resolved
Defining the SRE approach for vehicle-centric systems as Wayve scales programmes with partners such as Nissan, Stellantis, Mercedes and Uber.

🙌 You Should Apply If

You write production-quality code every day in Python, C++, or Rust
You’re comfortable debugging at the Linux and systems level, reading logs, tracing failures, and finding root cause in complex environments
You have experience with CI/CD, containerisation, networking, distributed systems, databases, and observability/incident-management tooling such as DataDog, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Splunk, Humio or similiar
You’ve diagnosed complex production or operational systems independently, seeing problems through to resolution rather than just escalating
You communicate well across engineering, operations, and field teams, and know when to bring others in
You can be onsite in Sunnyvale at least three days a week to work alongside the field teams you’ll support
Experience with autonomous vehicles, robotics, embedded systems, large-scale telemetry, or safety-critical environments is a plus, though not required

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More About Wayve

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)
Competency interviews Hiring-manager interview, including an abridged technical assessment (1 hour)
Deep-dive technical interviews Programing , System Design, and SRE Domain Knowledge (3 hours total)
Final interview: mission & values alignment (1 hour), including an onsite visit and demo ride.

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve

✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.
